To correct this, we first need to disable the ground collision setting. Right-click in the 3D window, go to Simulation Properties, and uncheck Collision Underground. If you prefer a cleaner workspace, you can turn off the ground grid from the left menu in the 3D window. Once these settings are adjusted, proceed with simulating the outfit onto the avatar. ### Modifying Outfit Details to Achieve Optimal Performance We need to adjust the mesh type, disable seam taping, and modify the top stitch texture. First, to convert the entire mesh of the outfit to quad, select all garments using Control + A, then go to the Property Editor on the right panel and set Mesh Type to Quad under Geometry. Next, disabling unnecessary seam taping can further optimize performance. Select all garments using Control + A and go to the Property Editor to find Selected Line and set Seam Taping to Off. Additionally, if the outfit has a top stitch, check its settings. If the stitch type is set to OBJ, it increases the mesh count, which may negatively impact performance. In this case, switching the top stitch to texture is recommended, as it helps reduce the mesh count and improves overall efficiency. Now that the outfit is set, let's move on to the next step: rigging. ## Rigging Once the outfit is fitted and all settings are finalized, open Everywhere by selecting Everywhere under Connect from the top to the bottom of the outfit menu. We will use the Garment tab in Everywhere to optimize the outfit, apply masking, and proceed with rigging polygon optimization. First, we will optimize the outfit. The recommended FBX mesh count is 20,000 polygons or fewer to ensure smooth processing. Enter 15,000 in the input field next to Garment and proceed with optimization. Once optimization is complete, resimulate the outfit. However, if the mesh expands after simulation, causing the outfit to clip into the avatar or behave unstably, it may be best to skip resimulation. Evaluate the results and decide whether to keep the simulation based on stability. ### Masking Next, we will remove unnecessary mesh areas through the masking process. Activate the masking brush by clicking the brush icon next to the Optimize button. Since AR filter outfits are designed in thin mode without thickness, we will only apply masking to the front side of the garment. Now use the brush tool to select the mesh areas you want to remove. If you need to unmask any part during the process, switch the mode to subtract to restore the masked areas. The masking brush can be used in both the 2D and 3D viewport, so feel free to work in whichever view is more convenient for you. ### Rigging Click Apply in the Rigging tab to proceed with auto rigging. If weight adjustments are needed, use the weight brush tools: Add, Subtract, and Smooth to refine the rigging. If the garment is penetrating the avatar or requires shape adjustments, utilize the sculpt brush tools: Grab, Smooth, and Fix Intersection to clean up the surface and refine the shape. Once all modifications are complete, click the Exit button to close the brush window. ## UV and Baking Once rigging is complete, navigate to the Material tab in the Everywhere window to begin the texture process.
